turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): In you come. I'll do the checks before Dr Keane sees you. Have a seat there.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. I hope I am not inconveniently early.

[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): You're grand, sure. My sister had a wicked dose of back pain after her little lad was born, and she couldn't sit in the car for months. Different story to yours, mind. Cuff's going on.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Right. Blood pressure is 132 over 78, pulse 74, oxygen 98 percent. That's all fine. He won't be long.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr Keane. Sorry, the morning list ran over a bit. What brings you in?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Good afternoon, doctor. I have a pain in my lower back which shoots down my right leg, from the back past the knee into the calf. It has been three weeks. Sitting at my desk brings it to seven out of ten, and walking eases it a little.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does the pain reach the foot?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It stops in the calf, and it does not go into the toes.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): How did it start? Was there a lift, or did it just arrive?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I lifted a box of files at the office. The ache began that evening. Well, actually, the shooting began the next morning.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Umm. Are you taking any tablets for the pain?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Ibuprofin, four hundred milligrams, three times a day, by mouth, with food, for the past two weeks.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ibuprofen, four hundred milligrams three times a day for the pain. Grand.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. That is correct.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has someone been at you about exercises?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): A colleague at the office showed me some stretches. I have been doing them in the evenings, as she advised.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do they help at all?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I would not wish to say they have made a difference.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I have not had a fever.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any cough?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any trouble passing water, or with the bowels, or numbness where you sit?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing of that sort.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): And your weight, have you lost any?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I have not weighed myself, so I cannot say.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you had the back imaged before, an x-ray or a scan?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): About two years ago they did an x-ray of the lower back. They said it was borderline, a bit of wear and tear. I was not given a figure.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Err, a borderline remark on an old x-ray isn't something I'd hang a diagnosis on. Lie back there. I'm going to lift the leg, a straight leg raise.

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right leg, the pain comes on at about forty degrees. Left side is clear to seventy degrees, no pain. Tender over the lower lumbar spine, and no weakness in the foot that I can find.

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): What I think is happening, thinking out loud, is the disc is irritating the nerve going down the right leg. Sitting tugs on that nerve, which is why it shoots. Your body isn't fighting an infection here, and the bone isn't the main event.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. Thank you for explaining it so carefully. Would a scan be required?

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not for now. I won't order an MRI yet. If it hasn't settled with the physio, we might do a lumbar MRI then. I'll refer you to physiotherapy, and I'll see you back in six weeks.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep moving, don't sit for hours, carry on with the ibuprofen with food, and only do those stretches if they don't stir the pain. If the leg gets weak, or you cannot pass water, don't wait the six weeks, come straight in.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly, doctor. I shall follow that, and I will not ignore a change of that kind.
[SEG0036] person_1 (NURSE): I'll send the physio form from the desk. Mind the step. My sister swears by her physio, but that's her own business.

spec.situation: Person with low back pain shooting down one leg for three weeks, worse sitting; takes ibuprofen; a colleague's advice on exercises; doctor examines straight-leg raise and plans physio, no scan yet.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Office work and desk sitting implied; current occupation not explicitly stated.
